body:
## Summary
On Air's live screen is a function of when the operator opened the poster, not of the run on air. Give the live feed its own resumable subscription (since:0 from the run in flight, the contract's own resume path), owned by the page's lifetime, so the scene is always foldEvents(run so far).

## Description
The screen's live scene is a module-level LiveFeed fed by the app-wide /events fan-out, and only while On Air's Layer1 is mounted (Poster.tsx:131-135, feed.ts:61-62,87). Open On Air mid-run and the fold starts from the first frame that happens to arrive: no stream_start meta (HUD says 'waiting for the stream'), no case file, no open poll, no foil. Leave On Air for Brain and come back, and every close_poll / dismiss_foil / reveal_hex in between is missing, so a closed poll and a dismissed foil stay on the operator's monitor. The daemon already solves this: a 'live' subscribe with since:0, run_id:'' backfills the run in flight with seq numbers that dedupe on resume (contract.md:411-414), and the console socket client implements it (socket.ts:104-140). Its only consumer is the app-wide stream, which started before On Air existed. openReplay, which opens exactly such a dedicated stream, has zero consumers.

Leans on realtime-events / subscription-lifecycle ('events arrive before any consumer attaches'; every subscription names its reaper, no zombie after the owner leaves) and push-vs-refetch-reconciliation (the push is truth only if the consumer saw all of it). The live feed becomes: subscribe while (Layer1 mounted AND source=live), fold every enveloped frame through stage-kit reduce with the seq cursor, reset on new run_id or stream_start, close on unmount or on switching to a stored run. A gap issue surfaces as HUD status instead of a silently wrong scene.

## Flow
- data/layer.ts: `openLive(onEvent, onIssue)`, a thin named wrapper over openEventStream('live') (openReplay stays for replays).
- player.ts: LiveFeed gains `reset()`, a `gap` flag in its snapshot, and applies frames by seq once.
- feed.ts: useOnAirFeed opens openLive in an effect keyed on (mounted, source.kind==='live') and disposes it on cleanup; the useLiveEvents push goes.
- Layer1.tsx: screenState reads the gap flag ('Live · missed events, catching up').
- Tests: new feed.live.dom.test.tsx on fakeSockets (mountPage exposes them), player.test.ts for seq dedupe and reset.

## Expected impact
The live monitor an operator watches during a run is correct on first open and after every page switch. The 'waiting for the stream' / 'Nothing is on air' false negatives during a live run disappear. Cost: one extra WebSocket while On Air shows Live, closed when it does not.

## Evaluation
Claim: the live scene equals the fold of the run in flight regardless of when On Air mounted.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (mid-run join folds from the join point; remount misses the gap; no page-owned socket exists)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first on the fakeSockets + manualTimers rig
Result: better
Gate: architecture (moves the live feed's ownership from the app-wide fan-out to a page-owned resumable subscription); no contract change, no policy change.
evidence: Poster.tsx:131-133 `{p.view !== "wall" && p.active && ( <Suspense fallback={null}> <Layer1 active={p.view === "l1"} />`; feed.ts:61 `/** The live feed folds every /events event while On Air is mounted. */`; feed.ts:87 `useLiveEvents((env) => live.push(env.event, env.runId));`; player.ts:193-195 `const fresh = (runId !== undefined && runId !== this.runId) || event.type === "stream_start"; ... const base = fresh ? initialScene() : this.snapshot.scene;`; view.ts:213 `: "waiting for the stream"`; contract.md:413-414 'sends "since": 0, "run_id": "" to get enveloped frames from the start of the run in flight'; socket.ts:107-108 `since: lastSeq ?? 0, ...(opts.target === "live" ? { run_id: lastRunId ?? "" } : {})`; grep -rn openReplay apps packages -> only apps/console/src/data/layer.ts:32 and :78.

critic.reason: Real, well-grounded live-scene correctness bug; one case is free-riding on existing socket dedupe.

revision: Drop acceptance case 4 (resubscribe replay applied once, scene.applied===80): socket.ts:135 already drops replayed seq, so it cannot distinguish a right build from a wrong one.

title: Replay is play/pause/restart: scrub, and jump the screen to any beat or moment
acceptance: ReplayPlayer paused at start, seek(30_000) -> snapshot.position === 30_000, scene equals foldEvents(events with ts_ms <= 30_000), playing stays false, timers.pending() is empty
ReplayPlayer playing at 90_000, seek(10_000) -> scene rebuilt (applied === count of events <= 10_000), playing true, exactly one timer pending, epoch bumped

Layer1 replaying a run: the progress bar is a role=slider with aria-valuemin/max/now in transcript time; ArrowRight -> position +5 s, ArrowLeft -> -5 s, Home -> start, End -> end (today: aria-hidden, no input)
the scrubber draws one band per stage-kit segmentSpans span and one tick per clipMarkers mark_moment; a 100k-line transcript keeps nodes() <= PAGE_L1
Rundown run detail: activate 'Play from here' on the beat at ts T (a start_poll) -> route is #/onair, the screen's snapshot.position === T and data-poll is set
clicking a segment span in RunDetail's timeline bar -> On Air plays that run from the span's start
source=live -> the scrubber is aria-disabled and LiveFeed.seek is a no-op

body:
## Summary
The On Air screen replays a real run, but the operator can only play, pause or restart it. The rundown already lists every beat with its time, yet no beat can be put on screen at that time. Add seek to the replay player and make it reachable three ways: a keyboard and pointer scrubber with segment bands and moment ticks, 'Play from here' on every beat, and clickable segment spans.

## Description
Today, to see what the screen looked like when a poll opened at 4:12, the operator restarts and waits up to a minute at 4x, or leaves the console for the broadcast stage, which already scrubs (apps/stage/src/App.tsx:142-149). The data for a jump is all present: beatsOf gives each beat's ts (RunDetail.tsx:76-83), segmentSpans and clipMarkers give bands and ticks (playback.ts:61), and Timeline.advanceTo rebuilds on a backward seek (playback.ts:35-47). The missing pieces are a seek verb on the player and a control that is not aria-hidden.

Leans on media-playback / playback-clock (one clock held outside reactive state: seek re-anchors the ReplayPlayer's single anchor, the scrubber derives from the snapshot, no second position variable; the 'needle snaps back mid-scrub' case is covered by emitting the seeked position before rescheduling) and transport-contract (a control never lies: on the live feed the scrubber is disabled, not an enabled no-op). Event-driven scheduling stays: seek clears the one timer and schedules the next due event, so the player still never ticks per frame.

## Flow
- player.ts: `seek(t)` on Feed; ReplayPlayer clamps, rewinds or advances the Timeline, re-anchors the clock if playing, bumps epoch, reschedules; LiveFeed.seek is a no-op.
- feed.ts: `selectSource(s, { at })` stores a pending seek applied when the player for that key is created or already exists.
- Layer1.tsx: Progress becomes Scrubber (role=slider, arrows 5 s, Home/End, pointer drag) with segment bands and moment ticks from stage-kit.
- RunDetail.tsx: 'Play from here' per beat row and clickable span segments call selectSource(run, { at }) and navigate to #/onair.
- Tests first: player.test.ts seek cases, scrub.dom.test.tsx for the slider and the beat jump, a DOM budget case in onair.dom.test.tsx.

## Expected impact
Inspecting any moment of a run takes one click from the rundown instead of restart-and-wait or a trip to the stage. The screen becomes a review instrument, not a loop.

## Evaluation
Claim: any beat, moment or segment start of a stored run can be put on screen in one action, by keyboard or pointer.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no seek verb; progress aria-hidden; beats link only to the transcript)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (manualTimers player rig, mountPage DOM tests)
Result: better
Gate: none (in-context UI; stage-kit is read, not edited). Shares feed.ts/player.ts with slot A: build sequentially, not in parallel.
evidence: player.ts:29-36 `export interface Feed { subscribe; getSnapshot; play(): void; pause(): void; restart(): void; dispose(): void; }`; Layer1.tsx:50 `<div className={styles.prog} aria-hidden="true" data-role="onair-progress">`; RunDetail.tsx:80-82 `<RouteLink to={pageRoute("brain", "transcripts", runId, String(b.line))} ...>L{b.line}</RouteLink>`; RunDetail.tsx:38 `role="img" aria-label={Segments: ...}`; feed.ts:56 `if (cur?.key === key) return;`; playback.ts:37-40 `if (t < this.appliedTo) { this.cursor = 0; this.state = initialScene(); }`; grep -rn clipMarkers apps packages (non-test) -> apps/stage/src/Controls.tsx:5,73 and packages/stage-kit/src/playback.ts:61 only; apps/stage/src/App.tsx:224 `else if (e.key === "ArrowRight") seek(clock.current + 5000);`.

critic.reason: Grounded, falsifiable UX elevation; schedule after slot A and shell-router A.
